entities.summary: Cayman Brac is an island that is part of the Cayman Islands. It lies in the Caribbean Sea about 145 km (90 mi) north-east of Grand Cayman and 8 km (5.0 mi) east of Little Cayman. It is about 19 km (12 mi) long, with an average width of 2 km (1.2 mi). Its terrain is the most prominent of the three Cayman Islands due to "The Bluff", a limestone outcrop that rises steadily along the length of the island up to 43 m (141 ft) above sea level at the eastern end. The island is named after this prominent feature, as "brac" is a Gaelic name for a bluff. Cayman Brac is a island. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cayman Brac's unique terrain and geological features have made it an important location for scientific research and tourism in the Caribbean. The island's limestone outcrop, 'The Bluff', has been studied by geologists and paleontologists due to its fossil-rich deposits.
